detailed_rationale:
Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services is a fintech/SaaS platform for employee spend management — prepaid corporate cards, expense management and rewards/incentive programs — a genuinely fast-scaling category with reported FY26 revenue of ₹1,908cr (up 46% YoY) and net profit of ₹139cr (up 58% YoY), continuing an acceleration visible across the last several quarters (₹26cr to ₹35cr to ₹37cr to ₹41cr net profit sequentially). On the reported income statement, this is one of the strongest growth stories in this batch, and I found no confirmed governance, SEBI or auditor-flag issue in the sources I was able to check.

What concerns me is the divergence between this reported growth and the company's cash generation and market reception: free cash flow was negative (₹-159cr, Mar-2026) despite the reported profit, operating margins are thin and flat (9-10%) for a business posting 46%+ revenue growth, borrowings have started rising, the company pays no dividend despite years of reported profitability, and — most tellingly — FII ownership has collapsed from 11.70% (Mar-2024) to just 2.31% (Jun-2026) while the stock itself has fallen 46% over the past year, even as reported growth stayed strong. That combination — foreign institutional investors exiting hard and the market pricing the stock down sharply despite headline growth acceleration — reads as the market pricing in a cash-quality-of-earnings concern that the reported P&L doesn't fully capture on its face. I don't have a confirmed specific cause (e.g., a disclosed related-party or revenue-recognition issue) from the sources I opened, so I'm not asserting one, but the pattern itself (strong paper profit, negative free cash flow, heavy smart-money exit, severe price decline) is a genuine tension worth a portfolio-manager look rather than a routine Hold.
recommendation_rationale: Quant reads Hold; my research doesn't find a confirmed fundamental breach that would justify overriding to Sell, but the cash-flow-vs-reported-profit divergence combined with the scale of the FII exodus and price decline is a genuine analytical tension I can't resolve from public disclosure alone, so I'm keeping the recommendation at Hold while escalating for a PM-level look rather than either forcing a Sell or waving the pattern away as ordinary.
summary: Zaggle is a fast-growing fintech platform for corporate spend management, and its reported revenue and profit have both grown strongly over the past year. However, the company generated negative free cash flow despite reporting a profit, pays no dividend, and has seen foreign institutional investors sharply reduce their holdings alongside a large decline in the stock price — a combination that suggests the market has real doubts about the quality of the reported earnings that the headline growth numbers alone don't show. We are flagging this for a closer look rather than treating it as a routine holding.
positive_para: Genuinely fast, broad-based reported growth (revenue +46%, profit +58% FY26) in a scaling fintech/spend-management category, with no confirmed governance or regulatory red flag found in available disclosures.
negative_para: Free cash flow was negative (₹-159cr) despite reported profit growth, margins remain thin (9-10%) for the growth rate claimed, no dividend has ever been paid despite sustained reported profitability, and FII holders have cut their stake from 11.7% to 2.3% over roughly two years while the stock fell 46% — a combination that looks like the market pricing in an earnings-quality concern the P&L alone doesn't reveal.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At roughly 20.5x trailing earnings the multiple looks inexpensive for the reported growth rate, but that math is only as good as the earnings quality behind it — given the negative free cash flow and heavy institutional selling, I would not describe this as cheap in any confident sense; the reverse-DCF only clears if the cash-conversion gap closes, which is unverified from here.
escalation_reason: Reported revenue/profit growth (46-58% YoY) diverges sharply from cash generation (negative FCF of -Rs159cr) and from the market's own read of the stock: FII ownership collapsed from 11.7% to 2.3% over roughly two years and the stock fell 46% despite the reported acceleration. I found no confirmed specific cause (no disclosed related-party or restatement issue in the sources checked), so I am not asserting fraud or a specific breach, but the magnitude of the cash-vs-paper-profit gap and the smart-money exit is a genuine Hold-vs-Sell tension the quant score (based on reported financials) cannot see, and it should get a PM-level look before further capital is added.
